content:
alex_sales: Quick sync — Acme just signed an enterprise commit. They want sizing guidance: 5k RPS sustained for chat completions, 20k RPS burst for marketing spikes, target p99 <200ms. They asked about reserved GPUs vs burst credits and how autoscale cooldowns affect latency. Can ops/infra weigh in?
maria_se: Congrats 🎉. High level: we should map RPS -> tokens/s -> GPU slots. Need avg tokens per request + model choice. Do we know model & avg tokens?@devon_engineer can you share POC profile?
devon_engineer: Their POC used redwood/gpt-neo-extended-13b quantized, avg request = 120 tokens, response 80 tokens (200 tokens total). Typical context length 512.
jordan_sre: Rough calc: 5k RPS * 200 tokens = 1M tokens/sec. With our benchmark for that model on aA100-equivalent slot = ~120k tokens/sec (with KV cache warm). So baseline reserve = ceil(1,000,000 / 120,000) = 9 slots. For bursts to 20k RPS -> 4x, so need 36 slots peak.
nina_prod: Important: that assumes warmed KV cache and steady-state. Cold-start or cache-miss increases CPU/GPU work and latency. For SLO we recommend reserved capacity sized to sustained + a 20% safety buffer (so 11 nodes), and burst handled by autoscale + burst credits.
alex_sales: Pricing question from Acme: how do burst credits price vs reserved monthly commit? They want example pricing for 11 reserved + burst to 36 for 2 hours/day typical.
maria_se: Pricing shorthand: reserved = committed monthly SKU (discounted). Burst credits are consumed per-GPU-hour above reserved at a premium rate. Example: 11 reserved @ discount = X/mo, peak burst (25 extra slots) * 2 hours/day * 30 days = 1500 GPU-hours billed at burst rate. I'll pull numbers from pricing doc and post later.
devon_engineer: One more operational caveat: autoscale cooldown = 3m by default plus scheduling time ~1-2m. For sudden 4x spikes you will see queueing unless prewarm or use preheat policy. Suggest preheat window tied to traffic signals or a steadying proxy that smooths bursts.
jordan_sre: If they need strict p99 <200ms during spikes we should avoid scaling during spike and instead rely on burst pool or prewarmed standby nodes. Autoscale reaction + cold scheduling will exceed SLO.
alex_sales: They also flagged security questionnaire Q12 about "dedicated GPU isolation" and "audit logging for autoscale events". security team ok to confirm? @security-bot any quick notes?
security-bot: Dedicated pools provide tenant isolation at GPU allocation level; control plane audit logs capture scale events and operator actions. We can export to customer's SIEM (S3/CloudWatch) and provide signed attestations. I'll attach sample wording in a follow-up message.
nina_prod: Operational runbook suggestions for handoff: 1) Reserve 11 slots (sustained + buffer). 2) Configure burst pool with 25 extra slots on pre-authorized billing. 3) Set preheat triggers for marketing campaign windows. 4) Keep autoscale cooldown at 3m, but set min_instances = reserved count so we never scale below reserved.
alex_sales: Can someone draft the short one-pager (capacity vs cost + tradeoffs) I can send to Acme procurement? Need by EOD. @maria_se @nina_prod
maria_se: I'll draft numbers + example pricing table.
devon_engineer: I'll add the KV cache warmup recommendation and a small snippet for their infra team.
jordan_sre: I'll add the SLO/latency proof points and fallback plan (model fallback to smaller quantized variant).
alex_sales: Awesome — thanks team. If we agree on reserves: 11 committed, 25 burst pool, preheat windows for scheduled campaigns, autoscale min = 11. I'll loop in Acme legal for the billing clause. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: NOTE: Submitted reservation request draft for 11 slots -> ticket #INC-4829. Autoscale policy draft saved to infra repo -> refs/infra/autoscale/acme-policy.yaml
security-bot: Uploaded sample SOC/attestation blurb to the shared drive: link=https://redwood.internal/sigs/acme/sec-attach (shared with alex_sales)
alex_sales: Filed — closing internal sync. Will post customer facing doc once maria shares pricing.
